title: HS Code Classification and Tariff Adjustment
summary: This thread tracks the administrative process of updating, correcting, and refining HS Code classifications and their associated tariff values or duty rates within customs instruments. Over time, the mechanism has shifted from simple code substitutions to more complex tariff value determinations and duty exemptions for specific industrial inputs.

evolution.legal_basis: Transitioned from Customs Act 1969 to the Customs Act 2023.
evolution.scope: Expanded from simple code correction to comprehensive tariff value management and industrial input regulation.

timeline.change: Direct substitution of specific HS codes for industrial headings.
Adjustment of percentage-based duty rates linked to HS code notifications.
Refinement of HS code entries within existing duty exemption tables.
Introduction of minimum value (tariff value) determination for specific HS codes.
Formalization of tariff value and customs duty structures under the new Customs Act, 2023.
Expansion of minimum value tables to include broader categories of bovine meat and milk powder.
Further expansion and correction of HS code entries for industrial raw materials (steel/metal).

Customs Act 1969: Section 20 of this Act provides the legal authority for the Government to amend existing customs notifications through statutory orders.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(2) of this Act provides the enabling power to the Government to issue amendments to customs and tax-related notifications.
S.R.O. 74-AIN/2005: This existing customs notification is subject to further amendment regarding specific tariff headings and sub-headings as specified in the current order.
Bangladesh Customs Tariff: The order modifies various tariff entries within the existing schedule, specifically replacing multiple HS codes related to metal pipes, cables, electrical machinery, and transport vehicles with updated classifications.

Customs Act 1969: Section 19(1) of this Act empowers the government to grant exemptions and make amendments to existing customs notifications.
Value Added Tax Act 1991: Section 14(1) of this Act provides the legal authority for the government, in consultation with the National Board of Revenue, to amend fiscal notifications in the public interest.
National Board of Revenue: The government is required to consult with the National Board of Revenue before exercising its powers to amend customs and tax notifications.
S.R.O. 157-AIN/2012: This existing customs notification is amended to adjust specific duty rates, clarify exclusions for machine parts, and update HS Code entries within the referenced table.
Bangladesh Customs Tariff: The table of HS Codes within the tariff structure is updated by adding new codes, replacing existing ones, and deleting obsolete entries to maintain accurate classification of goods.

Renowned Brand: This term refers to well-known, widely recognized, or famous brands in the context of this order.
General Brand: This term refers to any brand that does not fall under the definition of a Renowned Brand.

Renowned Brand: The term is defined for the purposes of this order to mean a famous, well-known, or widely recognized brand.
